package_info.package_versions: Vulnerable versions prior to patched releases (see Microsoft advisory for specifics)
package_info.why_malicious: The malicious item abuses the PidLidReminderFileParameter MAPI property to trigger an automatic NTLM authentication attempt to an attacker-controlled UNC path, resulting in credential (NTLMv2 hash) leakage without user interaction.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (upon receipt of calendar/task item email)
execution_context.file_location: PidLidReminderFileParameter property in Outlook calendar or task item (MAPI message property)

malicious_snippets.code_language: MAPI property (configuration, not code in the traditional sense)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the crafted message sets the PidLidReminderFileParameter to a malicious UNC path, causing Outlook to automatically attempt to fetch a sound file from the attacker's SMB share, which triggers NTLM authentication and leaks the user's NTLMv2 hash to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Setting a reminder sound to a remote UNC path controlled by an attacker is highly unusual and causes automatic authentication attempts, leaking sensitive credentials.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, reminder sounds are local files or trusted network resources, not arbitrary external UNC paths. Outlook should not attempt to authenticate to untrusted external SMB shares automatically.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: In rare cases, organizations might use network shares for reminder sounds, but these would be internal, trusted, and not exposed to the internet.
key_indicators: PidLidReminderFileParameter points to external UNC path
Automatic SMB authentication to untrusted server
No user interaction required for credential leak

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a calendar or task item with PidLidReminderFileParameter set to a malicious UNC path.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim receives the email and Outlook processes the item.

attack_chain.action: Outlook automatically triggers a reminder pop-up, which attempts to fetch the sound file from the specified UNC path.
attack_chain.leads_to: Outlook initiates SMB authentication to the attacker's server.

attack_chain.action: Victim's NTLMv2 hash is sent to the attacker's server via SMB authentication.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can capture the hash for offline cracking or relay attacks.

behavioral_signatures: Outlook items with PidLidReminderFileParameter set to external UNC paths
Automatic SMB authentication attempts to untrusted or external servers upon receipt of calendar/task items
NTLM credential leakage without user interaction
file_indicators: MAPI messages with PidLidReminderFileParameter property referencing \\external-server\share
Unusual calendar or task items with reminder sound set to network locations
network_indicators: SMB (port 445) connections to external/untrusted IPs triggered by Outlook
NTLM authentication attempts to non-corporate servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Outlook calendar or task items where the PidLidReminderFileParameter references an external UNC path. Alert on SMB authentication attempts from user workstations to external IPs, especially those triggered by Outlook processes. Use email security tools to scan for and quarantine items with suspicious reminder sound properties. Employ network monitoring to detect and block outbound SMB traffic to untrusted destinations.
